(1) the power of situations is enhanced when individuals are self-selected and selected by others, and (2) the power of the SPE is enhanced by the fact that it is both a self-selection situation and a selection-by-others situation, and that these two factors interact to enhance its power.

(a) people with certain personal dispositions are more likely to be attracted to, and selected for, positions of power; and (b) people with certain dispositions are also more likely to use their power in ways that are consistent with their dispositions.

the power of a situation is not a simple matter of a situation acting directly on individuals, but rather a complex interaction among the situation, individuals, and their selection of others.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
situations are powerful but that they do not act on a blank slate.
situations are more powerful than people think and that people are more powerful than situations think.
the power of situations is not just in the situation, but in the interaction of the situation with personal characteristics and the choices of participants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
situations are powerful because they are not only the result of self-selection and selection, but because they can change people's dispositions.
the power of situations is a function of both selection by the situation and self-selection.
situations are more complex than the simple model of the SPE, and that the power of situations is not a simple, one-way process of influence.
